format: perathos bundle v2 (bundle_version 2.0), NEXUS commerce event mapping
test_keys_note: FIXED TEST KEYS (RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 1-3), published on purpose. Never use them for anything real.

01-order-confirmed.description: seq 1 of the order: order.confirmed, the first event, so input_text is ""

02-order-shipped.description: seq 2 of the order: order.shipped, input_text is the previous event's bundle_id

03-order-delivered.description: seq 3 of the order: order.delivered, input_text is the previous event's bundle_id

04-dispute-closed.description: seq 4 of the order: order.dispute_closed with outcome 'won', input_text is the previous event's bundle_id

10-answer-edited.description: answer edited after signing; output_hash still binds the original payload.

11-output-hash-edited.description: output_hash edited; it is bound into integrity_hash.

12-trace-edited.description: _trace edited; it no longer hashes to trace_hash.

13-bundle-id-edited.description: bundle_id edited; it is uuid5(PERATHOS_NAMESPACE, integrity_hash).

14-forged-signature.description: A well-formed Ed25519 signature over integrity_hash from another key; verify_key still names the trusted key.
14-forged-signature.mutation: provider_signature.signature: made with the forger key; verify_key unchanged

15-signature-removed.description: No provider_signature; fails because signatures are required (require_signed / CLI default).

17-untrusted-signer.description: Built exactly like 01 but signed by the outsider key, which is not in jwks.json.

18-answer-stripped.description: answer removed. Python checks answer only when present, so verify_bundle returns (True, ""). NEXUS requires answer for model nexus.commerce.event/1 (TRUST_RECORD.md section 4.1, D3): without it the bundle carries only a hash and nobody can read what was attested.

19-chain-broken.description: seq 2 (order.shipped) built and signed correctly, but its input_text is not 01-order-confirmed's bundle_id (last hex digit changed). Python verifies one bundle at a time and accepts it; a chain check over [01-order-confirmed, 19-chain-broken] fails because input_hash != sha256(previous bundle_id).
